frequency_question: How often does a congressional joint resolution of disapproval successfully pass both chambers and survive or override a presidential veto to block a major executive foreign agreement?
membership_rule: Includes all formal congressional resolutions of disapproval introduced against major international nuclear cooperation agreements or major foreign military sales under statutory review procedures. Excludes non-binding resolutions and informal expressions of disapproval.

cases.name: Iran Nuclear Agreement Review Act (JCPOA disapproval attempt)
AECA disapproval of Saudi/UAE arms sales
AECA disapproval of weapons to Saudi Arabia (Yemen)

provenance_note: rate of 0% from only 5 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 5 major formal legislative disapproval votes on high-stakes Middle East executive agreements/sales since the post-Watergate statutory review mechanisms were established; zero have successfully overridden a presidential veto or successfully blocked the underlying transaction.
known_gaps: Excludes minor resolutions withdrawn before floor votes or cases where the executive modified the agreement prior to formal vote.
skeleton: Legislative veto / disapproval attempts under fast-track statutory provisions against executive foreign policy actions where presidential veto must be overridden (2/3 majority in both houses).
multiplier: 5 historical major challenges / 0 successful veto overrides blocking the executive action
validity_reason: The structural friction is anchored in Article I veto override thresholds (two-thirds of both chambers) and the constitutional balance of power, which changes very slowly over decades.
